gaps.sentence: The reason ___ the flight was diverted has never been made public.
gaps.explanation: 'The reason why' — 'why' is the relative for reasons.

gaps.sentence: The exam, the results of ___ will be published on Friday, was very difficult.
gaps.hint: quantity noun + of + thing in a non-defining clause
gaps.explanation: 'The results of which' joins the clauses formally; 'of whom' is for people and 'of them' cannot link clauses after a comma.

gaps.sentence: The woman ___ won the prize gave a short speech.
gaps.explanation: The gap is the subject pronoun for a person, so 'who' is needed; 'whose' would show possession.

gaps.sentence: The house ___ windows were broken has now been sold.
gaps.explanation: 'Whose windows' — the windows belong to the house.

gaps.sentence: They said nothing at all, ___ I found rather strange.
gaps.explanation: 'Which' here means 'and this'; it refers to the whole situation and follows a comma.

gaps.sentence: A nurse is a person ___ looks after patients.
gaps.explanation: 'Who' introduces a defining clause about a person performing the action.

gaps.sentence: ___ surprised me most was his calm.
gaps.hint: 'what' = the thing that; the sentence has no other subject
gaps.explanation: 'What' means 'the thing that' and acts as subject: 'What surprised me most ...' — 'that' cannot introduce this nominal clause.

gaps.sentence: I'll never forget the day ___ we first met.
gaps.explanation: 'When' replaces 'on which' after time nouns like day, year and moment.
